system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: WS-BCARTER-01 made multiple connections to the explicit proxy during the review period, including at 13:36, 13:41, 13:45, 13:48, 13:56, 14:01, 14:04, and 14:06 UTC. These records show connections to the proxy, but not the external destinations.
Just before the alert window, WS-BCARTER-01 successfully used the proxy to CONNECT to drive.google.com:443, an unapproved file-sharing service in the supplied inventory context.

At 13:46:51 UTC, the domain controller recorded a TGT request for ben.carter and a service-ticket request for WS-BCARTER-01$ from 10.30.10.24, rather than the .22 address associated with WS-BCARTER-01 in other records. The available records do not identify the .24 host.

At 14:11:54 UTC, just after the alert's stated 13:30–14:10 interval, DropboxUpdate.exe ran as SYSTEM on WS-BCARTER-01. Dropbox is not listed as approved, but this process event alone does not establish file synchronization or malicious activity.

At 14:13:33 UTC, Chrome on WS-BCARTER-01 attempted to CONNECT to login.microsoftonline.com and the proxy denied it; this is consistent with a blocked attempt to reach an approved service, not evidence of a successful connection.

known_telemetry_limitations: According to the supplied sensor-coverage metadata, WS-BCARTER-01 winsec and Sysmon collection, and proxy collection, were unavailable from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC—the central alert interval. That metadata has no record IDs.

The provided Zeek connection records during the interval identify the internal proxy as the destination, not the external HTTPS destinations. The missing proxy records prevent confirmation of those destinations from the supplied evidence (for example, T006-00157, T006-00275, T006-00300, T006-00319).
claims_not_established: The available records do not establish the external destinations or content of the proxy connections during the telemetry outage (for example, T006-00157, T006-00275, T006-00300, T006-00319).

The records do not establish that data was uploaded, downloaded, or exfiltrated during those connections; the observed Zeek byte counts are for connections to the proxy (for example, T006-00157, T006-00275).
The records do not identify which device used 10.30.10.24 or establish that the ticket requests from that address led to a successful logon (T006-00190, T006-00191).
The Dropbox process events do not establish when or how Dropbox was installed, whether it synchronized files, or whether it caused the alert-period connections (T006-00339, T006-00340).
The evidence does not establish that the periodic proxy connections were malicious or benign.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain the missing WS-BCARTER-01 winsec and Sysmon records and PROXY-HD-01 proxy logs for 13:30–14:10 UTC, including destinations, request details, and associated users or processes.

Identify the device assigned to 10.30.10.24 and review its authentication and endpoint records around 13:46:51 UTC, including whether any session to WS-BCARTER-01 was established (T006-00190, T006-00191).
Review available Zeek DNS and TLS records for WS-BCARTER-01 during the window to identify external destinations and certificates.
Determine the installation source and use of Dropbox on WS-BCARTER-01, and whether it generated network traffic or transferred files (T006-00339, T006-00340).
Validate whether the Google Drive connection was authorized for ben.carter or otherwise explain the access (T006-00016).
